newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Haider wants repatriation of foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Haider wants repatriation of foreigners.

text.p: Far-right leader Joerg Haider on Tuesday blamed the government for record unemployment and called for foreigners to be repatriated to provide more jobs for Austrians.

"I am concerned that new immigrants will take away jobs from Austrians and foreigners already living here," the Freedom Party leader told a news conference. "The government's policy is leading to more unemployment."

Unemployment hit 300,000 in January, the highest level since World War Two. Haider said the government had overstepped the quota of foreign workers in Austria by some 40,000 and demanded an urgent halt to this year's planned influx of 17,000 foreigners.
The govenment's policy on immigration was "management by chaos". The Social Democrat and conservative coalition government must adopt concrete measures to send foreigners home, Haider said.
This would be cheaper than supporting unemployed foreigners, when every unemployed person costs the state 240,000 schillings ($20,000), he added.
"We are not advocating throwing foreigners out by force but helping them to be reintegrated in their own countries," he said.
Green Party spokeswoman Terezija Stoisits rejected Haider's proposal and said repatriation was not the way forward.

"It is extremely easy using this scapegoat theory to blame someone and say this is the solution," she said. "Playing people off against each other will just jeopardise living together in this republic."
The Freedom Party last week caused a storm when a regional branch issued a directive to grant public building contracts only to firms that did not employ foreign workers.
Haider said the move had opened up a healthy debate on the issue.
"In a time of high unemployment it is absolutely right to think first of Austrians," he said on Monday in an interview with current affairs magazine Profil.

The social and interior ministers and regional party heads were the real lawbreakers and should be investigated for abusing their position, he told reporters. They were responsible for distributing over 300,000 work permits to foreigners, breaching the official 1996 quota of 265,000, he added.
Haider has won huge support for his anti-foreigner policies. In European Parliament elections last October the Freedom Party soared to an all-time high of nearly 28 percent.
